name: Fake model
note: Unit and IT tiers: the fake that stands in for the model. Every strong reference does all six; the Java ones are spring-ai, langchain4j and adk-java.

items.why: Matches U3 (double only at a boundary) and research/24. spring-ai, openai-agents and adk-java each ship one shared scripted fake; claude-agent-sdk's copied per-test fakes drifted apart (two fake CLIs report different versions).
Cheap and catches a loop that runs one turn too many or too few. spring-ai, adk-java and openai-agents all throw when the script runs out; openai-agents also fails on unused steps.

In Spock or JUnit this is a global extension, or a test-profile bean, that fails any real model client unless the spec is tagged live. openai-agents and pydantic-ai both guard this way; claude-agent-sdk and adk-python have no guard.

The main place loop bugs show: a lost tool result or broken history appears in the next request, not in the final answer. It is the positive form of V3 (no mock that implements the asserted behaviour).
Needed wherever adapters are hand-written over raw HTTP: a model-port fake never runs the request mapping. langchain4j (MockHttpClient), adk-java (FakeGeminiApi) and anthropic-sdk-java all do it.

Approve the rule, but merge it with LS12 when the reference is written: the same abstract contract suite runs at the IT tier against a fake HTTP server and at the live tier against the real provider (langchain4j: 33 methods, 43 provider classes).

name: Agent loop
note: How the loop itself is tested on the fake: errors, caps, streaming, retries, time.

items.why: Every strong reference asserts the error reaches the model and the run continues (anthropic-sdk-java, langchain4j, pydantic-ai, adk-python).
anthropic-sdk-java, adk-java and pydantic-ai test the cap; spring-ai's live IT has an unbounded while-loop, which is the failure this prevents.
spring-ai's scripted fake streams one chunk only, so its streaming tests never cross a chunk boundary; langchain4j joins partials and tool-call deltas and checks order.
mastra's mid-stream-drop scenario guards a real regression: the partial attempt was merged into the stored message.
The fixed-clock half is already U1 (repeatable: fixed clock). Keep only the new half: order races with explicit signals, never sleeps (openai-agents' guardrail race test).

name: Agent scenarios
note: One rule per agent scenario, each from the best fake-tier test found (research/70 section 2).

items.why: langchain4j evicts a tool call and its result together; spring-ai snaps to a turn boundary and keeps the system prompt.
spring-ai pins what is kept and what the summariser saw; adk-java pins that already-compacted history is never summarised again.
The strongest test found: pydantic-ai checks byte-stable prefixes over every capability and three providers, with a moving fake clock.
spring-ai caps Anthropic's 4 cache breakpoints and marks only the last tool result.
mastra keys on tenant and never caches errors; spring-ai includes the system prompt so personas don't share answers.
pydantic-ai keeps the response that crossed the limit, because it was already billed.
openai-agents asserts the blocked run made zero model calls, and that a rejected tool input never runs the tool.
openai-agents and adk-java resume from saved state and assert each side effect ran exactly once, including adversarial cases.
pydantic-ai names and prices the serving model. No Java reference tests fallback at all, so this fills a real gap.
No reference tests this, so it has no source: approve it only as an ours-rule, marked as such in the ledger, or leave it in Fog until we have a failure that shows it.

name: Recordings
note: Only applies to a project that replays recorded provider traffic. The JVM references hand-write payloads instead; these rules say how to do replay safely if a project chooses it.

items.why: pydantic-ai fails on unplayed interactions; mastra accepts a 60% fuzzy match with only a warning, the failure this prevents.
pydantic-ai scrubs credentials, tokens and account ids in pre-record hooks; mastra stores request bodies unscrubbed.

name: Live tests
note: Tests that call a real provider. Several rules overlap; the recommendations merge them so the reference keeps one rule per idea. The schedule (every PR first) is a project choice and lives in the project's docs/agents/testing.md.

items.why: The core rule of the tier: all ten references fake agent behaviour and go live only for acceptance, decisions, real chunking, and real usage and errors.
Merge with LT6 into one rule: one contract suite, run against a fake HTTP server in IT and against the real provider live.
langchain4j asserts maxOutputTokens(5) gives exactly 5 tokens and finish reason LENGTH; acceptance alone hides a dropped field.
Merge into LT15 as its tool-call example (exact arguments plus a stub-tool marker).
Real chunking is the most live-tested behaviour after basic chat: about 96 spring-ai classes and every langchain4j streaming provider.
Only the provider reports cache-write and cache-read tokens; spring-ai, langchain4j and pydantic-ai all assert them.
Merge into LT15 as its agent-level example (a bank balance, a routed sub-agent).

Keep everything except 'scheduled': a separate job with a pinned small model, a token cap and a protected secret, failing when skipped. Whether it runs per PR or nightly is the project's choice. Also absorb LS18.
Merge into LT14: pinning the model and failing on a missing key are the same rule.
Nobody asserts live prose; this becomes the one assertion rule, with LS14 and LS17 as its examples.
langchain4j retries every failure 3 times and spring-ai reruns twice, which hides flaky prompts; openai-agents injects the fault and asserts its own retry instead.
mastra's prefill test blanks its own key and always skips; two claude-agent-sdk tests assert nothing.
pydantic-ai's weekly model-catalogue check, with excluded names as strict expected failures; cheap and catches retired models.

name: Evals
note: Scored quality checks over repeated runs. A separate tier from live tests; none of the ten references blocks CI on an eval.

items.why: mastra's judge gives verdicts and code does the arithmetic; langchain4j counts NOT_SURE as failing; spring-ai's IT lets the generator grade itself, the failure this prevents.
adk-python versions thresholds per metric and aggregates by pass rate or minimum over runs; mastra fails a non-finite score.
